related_resources.reason: Biographical chronology, family, Far Rockaway and MIT/Princeton/Caltech; historical synthesis, including recollections attributed to later memoirs.
1918 birth, education, 1942 doctorate and marriage, wartime career and QED; available abstract, not full subscription-only biography.
Collection scope, correspondence, teaching and institutional posts; not a claim individual letters were inspected.
Caltech career summary; degrees, Cornell, basic discoveries, family archive donation.
Catalog description covering upbringing, training, Wheeler, nuclear project, QED, helium, weak forces and education; retrospective interviews.
Firsthand intellectual recollections and explicit admission of false starts; individual retrospective account, not complete independent chronology.
Prize co-recipients and official subject of award; note prize does not list all contributors.
Joan Feynman recalls childhood curiosity, brother, father, scientific work; retrospective first-person recollection.
Joan Feynman scientific achievements, childhood, family encouragement, career and education.
Research-based assessment of public persona, Los Alamos jokes, collaborators, gender and critical responses; some quoted views are retrospective and attributed.
Catalog description of 40 surviving letters and final weeks; not independent inspection of all autograph letters.
Review summary of Arline correspondence and later unsent letter; indexed PDF excerpt, not claim full letters were inspected.
Brazilian historical research for 1949 visit, 1951–52 stay, Tiomno, Leite Lopes, teaching, 1952 and 1963 talks; Brazilian contemporaries had their own scientific institutions.
Primary edition crediting Feynman, Leighton and Sands, 1961–64 recordings, 1964 Cornell Messenger Lectures and edition copyright limits.
Course curriculum and collaborators, wider Sputnik-era teaching reform, course dates and reception.
Family recollections from Joan and Michelle, colleague descriptions of informal Physics X discussions.
Feynman’s own public standard of reporting negative evidence and acknowledging uncertainties; cultural framing is historically specific.
1959 conceptual miniaturization proposals; not documentary evidence that all nanotechnology began with the talk.
Public communication of atoms and physical intuition; listed episode dates.
Risk estimates, reliability practice and management-engineering disconnect; primary authored appendix.
Solid rocket booster design, O-ring erosion, management warnings and accident causes; multi-investigator findings.
Commission record, chronology and hearings; not a claim each hearing transcript was separately read.
Historical absorber theory, its problem setting and collaborators; not modern standard theory by itself.
Path-integral formulation, amplitudes, action and Schrödinger equivalence; not claim that all interacting QFT path integrals are rigorous.
Diagrammatic rules and early renormalization program in QED; nonphysical internal lines not direct observed tracks.
Further mathematical validation of diagrammatic approach and all-order structure.
Equivalence and translation of QED approaches, including independent central contributions.
Early qualitative Bose liquid arguments and explicit limitations.
Phonon/roton spectrum and numerical mismatch explicitly noted in paper.
Collaboration, revised roton calculations and treatment of correlations.
Vector-minus-axial weak interaction theory, collaborative and subject to prior/parallel work.
Published 1958 paper documenting independent vector-axial weak interaction analysis; prior 1957 conference presentation described by authors and later historical scholarship.
Cobalt-60 parity experiment with coauthors, not exclusively Wu alone.
Gell-Mann/Zweig proposals, SLAC experiment teams, Bjorken scaling and Feynman parton model; multiple discovery lines.
Feynman’s parton picture at high energy, not sole origin of quarks or scattering evidence.
Quantum simulation motivation and state-space scaling; no claim Feynman alone invented subsequent quantum computing or hardware.
